Crew synchronization dictates the collective phase-space trajectory, transforming individual kinetic inputs into a coherent hydrodynamic thrust vector.
gsi_mapping: GSI models crew discipline as a low-entropy state. Bayesian inference updates the probability of capsizing based on asynchronous boarding vectors. primitives.name: Synchronized Descent Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ROWING 59 above the heads and the men on one sidethe side next the water—stepping under, and all grasping the cross-bars and swinging down to the water together.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: M: Total crew mass (kg); g: Gravitational acceleration (m/s^2); \tau: Synchronization time constant (s)
primitives.assumptions: Crew members act as point masses; gravitational field is uniform; cross-bars provide rigid constraint forces.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Desynchronization (\Delta \tau > threshold) leading to asymmetric torque and catastrophic capsize.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to coordinated multi-agent control systems where simultaneous state transitions prevent destabilizing moment arms.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in individual descent timestamps and resultant angular velocity of the hull.

primitives.name: Stability Gradient Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: The boat being in the water alongside the float, it is as well to say to the uninitiated that it is not advisable to jump into an eightoared racing shell in exactly the same careless manner in which the average excursion party boards a broadbeamed sail-boat.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \theta: Heel angle (rad); I: Moment of inertia (kg m^2); \delta: Hull beam width (m)
primitives.assumptions: Racing shell has minimal righting arm compared to broadbeam vessels; fluid displacement is instantaneous.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Impulsive vertical force application exceeding the metacentric height limit, causing \theta to approach \pi/2.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE risk assessment kernels evaluating impulsive load tolerances against narrow stability margins.
layer2.telemetry: Real-time heel angle deviation following discrete mass insertion events.

primitives.name: Structural Constraint Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: The feet should always be tightly strapped in the stretcher.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F_{strap}: Tension force (N); k: Stretcher stiffness (N/m); x: Displacement (m)
primitives.assumptions: Linear elastic response of the strap system; foot-stretcher interface friction is maximized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Strap slippage or material failure under peak drive-phase loads, decoupling rower from hull.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to boundary condition enforcement in finite element analysis, ensuring force transmission efficiency.
layer2.telemetry: Strain gauge readings on stretcher interfaces during maximum propulsive effort.

Mathematically, this is a problem of managing center-of-mass trajectories within a highly unstable potential well. The 'synchronized descent operator' derives from the necessity to minimize the temporal derivative of the hull's angular momentum during loading. If \sum \vec{r}_i \times \vec{F}_i \neq 0 due to staggered timing, the resulting torque instantly overcomes the minimal righting moment of the narrow beam. The 'stability gradient function' highlights the stark contrast between a broadbeam sailboat (wide basin of attraction) and a racing shell (infinitesimal basin). Jumping introduces a high-frequency impulsive force, mathematically modeled as a Dirac delta function applied off-center, guaranteeing a transition to the capsized attractor. Finally, the 'structural constraint matrix' ensures that once the system is in motion, the energy transfer from biological actuators (rowers) to the hydrodynamic medium is maximally efficient. The tight strapping eliminates compliance losses, acting as a rigid transformation matrix linking leg extension directly to hull propulsion. Together, these primitives form a complete state-transition model for safe and effective shell operation.
